---
title: "One day, open science – the housing-audit case"
subtitle: "Four parts of ninety minutes, with a facilitator"
---
This is the one-day course on the housing-audit case with open research in the foreground. It works on one field experiment, in which emails that differed only in the name that signed them were sent to public housing authorities in the United States, and on a claim of the original authors (OAs) that five analysts reanalysed for Multi100. In the morning you meet the arguments and the evidence on the credibility of social science, the three kinds of repetition that go under the word 'replication', and the archives and registries in which open research keeps its materials. You then read the paper and its claim with the five analysts, and write the estimand statement behind the claim. In the afternoon you reproduce one of the five reanalyses, whichever you choose, and find out what a reproduction needs besides data and code. You end on the replication that tested the claim with new data, read its preregistration, and fill in a preregistration block of your own without running it.

You leave able to tell the three operations of 'replication' apart and to read a replication report against its preregistration. You also take away one or two reanalyses that you reproduced yourself and a preregistration block of your own, filled in before any result existed. The day has no menu of specifications and sends nothing to a class chart, because the [one-day course on methods](../housing-one-day-methods/index.qmd) does both.

## How you work

The day is taught mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with nothing to install. Open it in a tab of its own and keep this page open beside it. Each part of the day has a page that lists its steps in order, and every step that you work at the keyboard has a button that opens the lab at the right task. If you have installed R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), the downloadable workspace holds the same tasks and gives the same numbers, and the setup page explains how to install it. The slides are on the [slides page](slides.qmd), and each part opens with a link to its place in the deck.

[Open the browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The class writes its estimand statements and its reproduced values in the chat and sends them at the same moment, so the day needs a facilitator.

## The parts of the day

- **[Before the day](before.qmd)** (about an hour, more with the installation). You read the case study and open the browser lab once, and you install R, an IDE and the workspace if you want to work there.
- **[Part 1 – Credibility and open research](part-1.qmd)** (ninety minutes). The part asks what a claim is for and why the field talks of a crisis, then covers the three Rs and the practices of open research, SCORE and Multi100, and the software, archives and registries of open research, and it ends with the browser lab running on your machine.
- **[Part 2 – The claim and its estimand](part-2.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after a break of thirty minutes). You meet the paper and the five analysts and two studies on why analysts disagree, and you write the estimand statement in Task 2.
- **[Part 3 – Reproduction](part-3.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after an hour for lunch). You reproduce one of the five reanalyses, find out what a reproduction needs, and reproduce a second one if there is time.
- **[Part 4 – Replication and preregistration](part-4.qmd)** (ninety minutes, after a break of thirty minutes). You meet the new audit and its preregistration and the public record of the case, and you fill in a preregistration block without running it.
- **[After the day](after.qmd)** (as long as you like). The page says where to go next.

[Start with Before the day](before.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

The same case is also taught as a [short session](../housing-short/index.qmd) and as one-day courses on [data tools](../housing-one-day-data-tools/index.qmd) and on [methods](../housing-one-day-methods/index.qmd).
